rows: Orders need to be persisted between restarts. The service runs on one host.
We will store orders in an embedded SQLite database owned by `OrderStore`.
No separate database server is needed, but the service cannot scale out.
We need to record the architectural decisions made on this project.
We will use Architecture Decision Records, as described by Michael Nygard.
Every significant decision gets a short record in docs/adr.
Zero and negative totals have reached the ledger and broken reconciliation.
`OrderService.placeOrder` rejects any order whose total is not positive.
Refunds must be modelled as their own transactions, not as negative orders.
Date: 2024-06-15 Deciders: Ana Lima, Ben Okafor
Accepted Supersedes [2. Store orders in SQLite](0002-store-orders-in-sqlite.md)
The service now runs on several hosts behind a load balancer, so an embedded database no longer works.
We will store orders in a managed PostgreSQL database, accessed only through `OrderStore`.
Every host shares one source of truth. The team must operate a database server and run migrations.
